```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(echarts4r)
library(vehicletrends)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(crosstalk)
library(plotly)
library(DT)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.path = "figs/",
  fig.width = 7.252,
  fig.height = 4,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.retina = 3
)

sp <- function(gap = 2, unit = "em") {
  sprintf('<div style="height: %s%s;"></div>', gap, unit)
}

rungbar <- function(n) {
  labs <- c(
    "a chart",
    "linked charts",
    "a box",
    "Shiny in the box",
    "anything in the box"
  )
  grp <- c("in", "in", "box", "box", "box")
  steps <- vapply(
    seq_along(labs),
    function(i) {
      sprintf(
        '<div class="rs rs-%s%s"><span class="rs-n">%d</span>%s</div>',
        grp[i],
        if (i == n) " is-on" else "",
        i,
        labs[i]
      )
    },
    character(1)
  )
  htmltools::HTML(paste0(
    '<div class="rungbar">',
    '<div class="rg rg-in">inside the document</div>',
    '<div class="rg rg-box">in a box</div>',
    paste(steps, collapse = ""),
    '</div>'
  ))
}
```

## Interactivity from a code chunk in [{{< fa brands r-project >}}]{.blue} or [{{< fa brands python >}}]{.yellow}

::: {.col width="50%"}
[**R**]{.blue} via {echarts4r}

::: {.font70}
```r
penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  e_charts(bill_length_mm) |>
  e_scatter(flipper_length_mm)
```
:::

[**Python**]{.yellow} via {plotly}

::: {.font70}
```python
px.scatter(
  penguins,
  x = "bill_length_mm",
  y = "flipper_length_mm",
  color = "species"
)
```
:::
:::

::: {.col width="50%"}
```{r}
penguins |>
  tidyr::drop_na(bill_length_mm, flipper_length_mm, species) |>
  group_by(species) |>
  # Square canvas, set explicitly rather than left to the column width, so the
  # aspect ratio doesn't move if the 60/40 split ever changes. 560 is what fits
  # under the rung bar and the title on a 900px slide.
  e_charts(bill_length_mm, width = "600px", height = "560px") |>
  e_scatter(flipper_length_mm, symbol_size = 9) |>
  e_color(c("#00798c", "#A77400", "#d1495b")) |>
  e_legend(bottom = 0, textStyle = list(fontSize = 16)) |>
  e_tooltip() |>
  # scale = TRUE drops echarts' default "always include zero" on a value axis,
  # which otherwise parks the whole cloud in the top-right corner. boundaryGap
  # then pads the data range by 5% so the points don't touch the frame.
  e_x_axis(
    name = "Bill length (mm)",
    scale = TRUE,
    boundaryGap = c("5%", "5%")
  ) |>
  e_y_axis(
    name = "Flipper length (mm)",
    nameLocation = "middle",
    nameGap = 45,
    scale = TRUE,
    boundaryGap = c("5%", "5%")
  ) |>
  e_grid(left = 80, right = 30, top = 20, bottom = 80)
```
:::

## [Widgets that talk to each other: `crosstalk`]{.center}

::: {.font55}
```{r}
# Two plots over one SharedData, with a dropdown and a slider above them, so the
# slide reads as a small app rather than as two widgets that happen to share a
# page. The table this replaced made the same crosstalk point but looked like a
# report; a second plot makes the linking visible, because a selection in one
# panel is legible in the other.
#
# `dragmode = "select"` matters on stage: without it a drag pans the plot and the
# audience never sees the link unless you first find the box-select button in the
# modebar. With it, drag a box and both panels respond.
pen <- palmerpenguins::penguins |>
  tidyr::drop_na(
    bill_length_mm,
    bill_depth_mm,
    flipper_length_mm,
    body_mass_g,
    species
  )
shared <- SharedData$new(pen)

pal <- c("#00798c", "#A77400", "#d1495b")

panel <- function(x, y, xlab, ylab) {
  plot_ly(
    shared,
    x = x,
    y = y,
    color = ~species,
    colors = pal,
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",
    marker = list(size = 8, opacity = 0.8),
    # ~515px wide in a 78% column, so 460 tall lands close to square
    height = 460
  ) |>
    layout(
      showlegend = FALSE,
      dragmode = "select",
      xaxis = list(title = xlab),
      yaxis = list(title = ylab),
      margin = list(l = 60, r = 10, t = 10, b = 50)
    ) |>
    highlight(
      on = "plotly_selected",
      off = "plotly_deselect",
      color = "#2e4057"
    )
}

htmltools::div(
  style = "display:flex; gap:1.6rem; align-items:flex-start;",

  # Controls stacked in their own left column, slider over dropdown. Stacking
  # them beside the plots instead of above is what makes the slide read as an
  # app: a control rail is the shape people recognise, and it buys the plots
  # enough height to come out roughly square.
  htmltools::div(
    style = "flex:0 0 22%; padding-top:0.6rem;",
    filter_slider(
      "mass",
      "Body mass (g)",
      shared,
      ~body_mass_g,
      width = "100%"
    ),
    htmltools::div(
      style = "margin-top:1.2rem;",
      filter_select("sp", "Species", shared, ~species)
    )
  ),

  htmltools::div(
    style = "flex:1 1 78%; display:flex; gap:1.2rem;",
    htmltools::div(
      style = "flex:1 1 50%;",
      panel(
        ~bill_length_mm,
        ~flipper_length_mm,
        "Bill length (mm)",
        "Flipper length (mm)"
      )
    ),
    htmltools::div(
      style = "flex:1 1 50%;",
      panel(~body_mass_g, ~bill_depth_mm, "Body mass (g)", "Bill depth (mm)")
    )
  )
)
```
:::

## [Or recompute in the browser: `ojs`]{.center}

```{r}
#| echo: false
ojs_define(
  pen_ojs = palmerpenguins::penguins |>
    tidyr::drop_na(
      bill_length_mm,
      bill_depth_mm,
      flipper_length_mm,
      body_mass_g,
      species
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(
      species,
      bill_length_mm,
      bill_depth_mm,
      flipper_length_mm,
      body_mass_g
    )
)
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Deliberately the SAME app as the crosstalk slide -- same two panels, same
// slider, same dropdown -- so the difference between the two slides is the
// machinery, not the picture.
//
// OJS is a dataflow runtime, so these two cells can be declared before the
// inputs they depend on. `output: false` keeps their values out of the slide.
data = transpose(pen_ojs)
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
filtered = data.filter(
  d => d.body_mass_g >= mass && sp.includes(d.species)
)
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// One plot definition used twice, so the two panels are provably the same call
// with different columns.
panel = (x, y, xlab, ylab) => Plot.plot({
  width: 520,
  height: 460,
  marginLeft: 60,
  marginBottom: 50,
  x: {label: xlab, labelAnchor: "center"},
  y: {label: ylab, labelAnchor: "center"},
  color: {domain: ["Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"],
          range: ["#00798c", "#A77400", "#d1495b"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.dot(filtered, {x: x, y: y, fill: "species", r: 4.5, fillOpacity: 0.8})
  ]
})
```

:::: {.col width="22%"}
::: {.font55}
```{ojs}
viewof mass = Inputs.range(
  [2700, 6300],
  {step: 50, value: 2700, label: "Body mass (g)"}
)
```

```{ojs}
// multiple: 3 makes this a list box with all three rows visible and everything
// selected at rest -- the same behaviour as crosstalk's filter_select. Plain
// `multiple: true` would open with NOTHING selected, i.e. an empty plot.
viewof sp = Inputs.select(
  ["Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"],
  {multiple: 3, value: ["Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"], label: "Species"}
)
```
:::
::::

::: {.col width="39%"}
```{ojs}
panel("bill_length_mm", "flipper_length_mm",
      "Bill length (mm)", "Flipper length (mm)")
```
:::

::: {.col width="39%"}
```{ojs}
panel("body_mass_g", "bill_depth_mm",
      "Body mass (g)", "Bill depth (mm)")
```
:::

## [Anything bigger goes in a box]{.center}

<br>

::: {.font70}
```r
htmltools::tags$iframe(
  src    = "https://vehicletrends.github.io/hhi-map/",
  height = "700px",
  width  = "100%",
  style  = "border: none;"
)
```
:::

<br>

[Six lines. That's the **entire** interface between the page<br>and whatever is on the other end.]{.font130 .blue}

::: {.notes}
Everything so far lives inside the document. Here's where that stops.

**This is the one slide where the bar is worth a glance.** The colour changed,
and it changed here for a reason: everything to the left of that line is
something Quarto gives you. Everything to the right is something Quarto
*composes*.

The slide itself is six lines, and they are the entire contract between a Quarto
page and something that isn't one. The page says *where*. It never says *what*.

Fifteen seconds. Don't dwell -- it's a hinge, not a destination. The next two
slides are what it holds.
:::

## [Yes, you can still use Shiny]{.center}

::: {.col}
[**Shinylive** -- no server]{.blue}

````markdown
```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 800
```
````

Compiled to WebAssembly, running in the reader's browser. Two pages on my site
are exactly this.
:::

::: {.col}
[**A real Shiny server**]{.red}

::: {.font55}
```r
tags$iframe(
  src = "https://shiny.example.com/explorer",
  height = "700px", width = "100%"
)
```
:::

When WASM isn't enough -- a database, data too big to ship -- deploy it and
point at it.
:::

<br>

[Same six lines either way. **The page can't tell the difference.**]{.font130 .blue}

## [Same strategy works for custom widgets!]{.center}

::: {.col width="58%" .font80}
<center>
```{r}
htmltools::tags$iframe(
  src = "https://vehicletrends.github.io/hhi-map/",
  height = "500px",
  width = "900px",
  style = "border: none;"
)
```
</center>
:::

::: {.col width="42%"}
- **276 lines** of hand-written MapLibre 
- **1.64 GB** of tiles built with `{pmtiles}` (thanks [Kyle Walker](https://walker-data.com/)!)
- Lives in it's [own repo](https://github.com/vehicletrends/hhi-map) 
- Hosted on [GitHub pages](https://vehicletrends.github.io/hhi-map/)
:::

---

## It's just static files

Everything here runs in the browser, and the whole site is files — **hosted for free.**

- charts → ECharts (JS), rendered client-side
- the map → PMTiles on a CDN, instant
- the Shiny app → **Shinylive**, compiled to WebAssembly. No server.

A GitHub Action re-renders and republishes it **every Sunday at 5am.** Nothing is
cached, so nothing goes stale.

[No server to run. No server to secure. No server to pay for.]{.font120}

{{< include svg/experiment.qmd >}}

::: {.notes}
Two ways to ask for the same document.

Top: three separate asks, three finished artifacts, and that's the end of the
chain. Bottom: same agent, one `.qmd`, and render fans out to the same three.

---

{{< inverse >}}
{{< center >}}
{{< middle >}}

<center>
<img src="images/fig-tokens.png" width=100%>
</center>

::: {.notes}
The agent pays for every character.

And it compounds over turns: about 81,000 tokens versus about 11,000 after ten
edits. The ratio never moves — the gap does.

The sharper version of the whole cost argument, worth saying out loud right
here: **it is not that markdown is smaller — it is that you stop paying for the
parts you did not change.** Character count is the proxy; regeneration is the
mechanism.
:::

And here's what I did **not** do: I did not regenerate the site. Nothing decided
the sidebar again, or the theme again, or the fourteen pages I never opened.
There is no version of this where the navigation quietly comes back different —
the same way there was no version of the worksheet where the layout drifted.

The numbers on those other pages aren't in these files either — that's

## [To change one thing, what has to agree?]{.center}

<br>

::: {.col}
[**in an app**]{.red}

- the **input** that defines it
- the **output** that consumes it
- the **reactive** that connects them

[Three places, and they have to match.]{.font110}
:::

::: {.col}
[**in a page**]{.blue}

- the **chunk**

`r sp(1)`

[One place, and it's the one<br>I'm already looking at.]{.font110}
:::

<br>

[This isn't about how much you write. It's about how much has to be true at once —]{.font120}

[and *that* is what an agent has to hold in its head.]{.font130 .blue}

::: {.notes}
Here's the version of that which actually matters for an agent.

An application is a coupled thing, and it should be -- that coupling is what
makes it reactive. But it means adding one filter touches an input, an output,
and the reactive expression between them, and all three have to agree.

A page isn't coupled. Adding a filter is a chunk.

**The line to land:** this is not a claim about how much code you write. It's a
claim about how much has to be simultaneously true -- and that is exactly what
an agent has to hold in context to make a change safely.

Which is the same argument as the next slide, one level down. If you're running
that one too, this is the handoff: *"and it scales."*

Note there is no comparison of volume anywhere on this slide, and no number.
Nothing here says an app is worse. It says an app is *coupled*, which is what
an app is for.
:::

# [Quarto is checkable twice]{.center}

<br>

::: {.col .fragment}
## [**By machine**]{.darkgreen}

### `quarto render` is a compile step

<pre class="specimen errcard">
<span class="sp-dim">Quitting from index.qmd:12-30 [africa-map]</span>
<span class="sp-err">Error:</span>
<span class="sp-err">! all(funding$name %in% africa$name) is not TRUE</span>
<span>Execution halted</span>
</pre>

:::

::: {.col .fragment}
## [**By human**]{.darkgreen}

### Plain text means the edit is a **diff**

<pre class="specimen diffcard">
<span>  ## EV Sales</span>
<span> </span>
<span>  Sales of **electric vehicles** grew 20% in 2025,</span>
<span class="sp-del">- reaching <span class="w">over</span> _20 million_ sales globally.</span>
<span class="sp-add">+ reaching <span class="w">nearly</span> _20 million_ sales globally.</span>
</pre>

:::

::: {.notes}
By machine: `quarto render` is a compile step, and an assertion can
fail the build.

By human: plain text means the edit is a diff. Review scales with the change,
not with the document.
:::

## [HTML is good, but it can't tell you if it's broken]{.center}

::: {.col .fragment}
[**HTML** - _manual_ numbers]{.red}

::: {.font140}
<pre class="specimen diffcard compact">
<span>  &lt;!DOCTYPE html&gt;</span>
<span>  &lt;html lang="en"&gt;</span>
<span>  &lt;head&gt;</span>
<span>  &lt;meta charset="utf-8"&gt;</span>
<span>  &lt;title&gt;EV Sales&lt;/title&gt;</span>
<span>  &lt;style&gt;</span>
<span>  body { font-family: Georgia, serif;</span>
<span>         max-width: 40em; margin: 3em auto; }</span>
<span>  h2 { font-size: 1.6em; }</span>
<span>  &lt;/style&gt;</span>
<span>  &lt;/head&gt;</span>
<span>  &lt;body&gt;</span>
<span>  &lt;h2&gt;EV Sales&lt;/h2&gt;</span>
<span>  &lt;p&gt;Sales of &lt;strong&gt;electric vehicles&lt;/strong&gt; grew</span>
<span class="sp-del">- 20% in 2025, reaching over &lt;em&gt;<span class="w">18 million</span>&lt;/em&gt;</span>
<span class="sp-add">+ 20% in 2025, reaching over &lt;em&gt;<span class="w">20 million</span>&lt;/em&gt;</span>
<span>  sales globally.&lt;/p&gt;</span>
<span>  &lt;/body&gt;</span>
<span>  &lt;/html&gt;</span>
</pre>
:::

:::

::: {.col .fragment}
[**`.qmd`** - _computed_ numbers]{.blue}

::: {.font140}
<pre class="specimen diffcard compact">
<span>  ## EV Sales</span>
<span> </span>
<span>  Sales of **electric vehicles** grew</span>
<span>  20% in 2025, reaching over</span>
<span class="sp-del">- _<span class="w">20 million</span>_ sales globally.</span>
<span class="sp-add">+ _<span class="w">&#96;r ev_sales&#96; million</span>_ sales globally.</span>
</pre>
:::

:::

::: {.notes}
Why not just ask for HTML? Agents are very good at it.

Because malformed HTML still renders as *something*, so the agent can't tell
whether it succeeded.

Left: nineteen lines, and the changed row has somewhere to hide. Right: compute
it once and never re-type it.
:::

## Where this gets annoying

- agents invent chunk options that don't exist — `quarto render` catches it, but only if you make them run it
- Quarto's errors point at the **rendered** line, not always the line you wrote
- a big render loop is slow; cache it or the agent will wait, and so will you
- models still write 2023-era Quarto — expect `output:` where you wanted `format:`

[None of these are fatal. All of them are cheaper than re-prompting a PDF.]{.font120}

::: {.notes}
NEW SLIDE — RECOMMENDED. Edit the four bullets down to whatever actually bit
you; the specific gripes matter less than the fact that you have some.

This buys credibility with the skeptic in row three, and it makes the next
slide read as mitigation rather than boilerplate. A talk that admits nothing
gets argued with in the hallway.

Keep it fast — twenty seconds, no dwelling. The last line is the whole point of
the slide.
:::

---

## Make this work Monday

1. Put *"always run `quarto render` before finishing"* in your `CLAUDE.md`
2. Have the agent work on a branch, so edits arrive as diffs
3. Keep data in files the `.qmd` reads — never in the prompt

::: {.notes}
Three things you can do Monday.

Read them fast. If you added the caveats slide before this one, these three now
read as mitigations, which is a better register than advice.
:::

# Quarto wasn't built for this.

[Nobody was thinking about agents in 2022.<br>]{.font120}
[It works anyway — that's the unreasonable part.]{.font120 .orange}

::: {.notes}
NEW SLIDE — RECOMMENDED. This is the title finally paying off, and it pays off
at the end rather than the beginning, which is where you wanted it.

"Unreasonable effectiveness" is Wigner's phrase, and it means a thing works far
better than its designers had any right to expect. That is exactly the claim:
the separation of content from format was built for reproducible research, and
it happens to be the correct architecture for a probabilistic author nobody had
met yet.

Do not explain Wigner. Just say the two lines and go to the last slide.
